facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Jim sailed home with the treasure. Silver ran away during the trip. Jim was different now. Every adventure teaches something important.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: Jim and his friends loaded the treasure and set sail for home. During the voyage back, Silver secretly escaped with some gold coins. Jim was angry but also understood that people do not change easily. What mattered most was that Jim himself had changed for the better. Every adventure teaches something important. Every experience on this adventure shaped who Jim became.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: With the treasure safely aboard, the Hispaniola began its long journey back to England. Jim stood on the deck and watched the island grow smaller on the horizon. During the return voyage, Silver managed to escape one night, taking a bag of gold coins. Jim felt conflicted — angry at Silver's treachery yet somehow understanding his nature. Every adventure teaches something important. However, the most significant change was not in the treasure they carried but in Jim himself. Because of everything he experienced, Jim had transformed from a timid boy into a wise young man. He realized that the true value of any journey lies not in the destination but in who you become along the way.
